item.text: The selected scope resolves to chapter 1B only (`selected_theme_ids: ["1B"]`), so I’m keeping this pass bounded to that chapter while covering all ten lenses. The search recovered direct 2022 nuclear/nonproliferation and CBRN-governance records, plus contrary civil-nuclear safety and implementation concerns. I’m now consolidating them into non-scoring evidence units and checking the write path once more.

Completed the bounded continuation for the only selected chapter, 1B. No score was assigned.

Recovered evidence units E034–E041:

- E034: Philippines’ August 2022 NPT statement reaffirmed IAEA safeguards, nonproliferation, and disarmament commitments. [UN statement](https://estatements.un.org/estatements/14.0447/20220808/fXus8bNLDpjV/VTBJRGBG7e2l_en.pdf), pp. 1–2.
- E035: October 2022 Philippine UN statement documented CWC/BWC implementation, UNSCR 1540 compliance, strategic-trade controls, and CBRN exercises. [UN mission statement](https://www.un.int/philippines/statements_speeches/thematic-debate-cluster-2-other-weapons-mass-destruction), paras. 4–8.
- E036: Philippines participated in the May 2022 OPCW regional implementation meeting. [OPCW](https://www.opcw.org/media-centre/news/2022/05/asian-member-states-strengthen-regional-cooperation-advance), paras. 1–3. Context only.
- E037: November nuclear-power planning remained conditional on third-party safety review, regulatory frameworks, social acceptance, and financing. [PPP Center](https://ppp.gov.ph/in_the_news/govt-mulls-ppp-for-nuclear-power/), paras. 4–11.
- E038: Greenpeace raised contrary concerns about nuclear waste, safety, cost, environmental harm, and community exposure. [Greenpeace](https://www.greenpeace.org/philippines/press/11980/nuclear-to-worsen-power-price-woes/), paras. 1–8, 10–14.
- E039: Philippine environmental groups opposed Marcos-era civil-nuclear cooperation, citing safety, waste, earthquake, affordability, and community risks. [GMA News](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/852398/green-groups-say-nuclear-energy-risky-harmful-to-philippines/story/), paras. 1–8.
- E040: July 2022 survey evidence showed public support but meaningful polarization over nuclear construction. [PIA](https://mirror.pia.gov.ph/press-releases/2022/07/01/59-support-allowing-construction-of-nuclear-plant-in-ph-publicus-survey), paras. 1–4, 8–10.
- E041: December cyber assessment identified governance, workforce, coordination, and implementation gaps, including recommendations reporting to the President. [PNA](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1190327), paras. 12–19.

Remaining shortfall: no inspectable 2022 evidence was found for nuclear command-and-control practice, nuclear crisis/threat/proliferation conduct, 2022 IAEA inspection outcomes, biological-risk enforcement, or AI-specific high-risk governance.
